title: Recording with Bunk Johnson in New York, 1945
summary: Purnell did not play with Oliver but recorded with Bunk Johnson; in 1945 Bunk took over the George Lewis band, giving Purnell his first travel outside the South. They guess when Bunk died.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I'll get one from him before we quit. Alton, I've heard a lot of your records going way back, I think. I don't know whether you ever played with Oliver on Snagit, of which I've got a copy at home, but I'm sure you were back in there somewhere.
No, I didn't play with Oliver, but I made Snagit with Bunk Johnson, which is one of the old trumpet players around Oliver's age, you know.

Well, Bunk Johnson, if I remember correctly, the records I've got of his, he made with Lou Waters up at Hambone Kelly some years ago after they rediscovered Bunk. You know, they found him pitching cotton or something. I don't know what he was doing, but they brought him a new set of teeth and brought him a trumpet, and away we went.

Yeah, this is the time, around the time I played him, but we were in New York, but we played in 1945, and we made a lot of records while we were there that were very good records. And it's too bad, I mean, Bunk had to pass away, you know, because this was my first chance to do any kind of traveling outside of the South by playing along with Bunk. See, Bunk hired the George Lewis band, which we all played together, and he was just a new man in the band. And so when Bunk came in and accepted our band to play with him, then they named it Bunk Johnson's band.
Yeah, boy, it could play an awful lot of instrument, that fella.
Yeah, Bunk was a pretty good old man.
Oh, five years ago, was it? Well, no, it was longer than that. Bunk died in the 50s, or maybe in the 40s. I don't know, around 50s, late 40s or 50s.
